steps.title: Define the Orthonormal Bernstein Basis
steps.instruction: Construct the shifted orthonormal Bernstein polynomials $B_{i,n}(x)$ over the interval $[0, 1]$ using the Gram-Schmidt procedure on the set of Bernstein polynomials $b_{i,n}(x)$.

substeps.instruction: Define the standard Bernstein polynomials: $b_{i,n}(x) = \binom{n}{i} x^i (1-x)^{n-i}$ for $0 \le i \le n$.

Represent the orthonormal basis $B_{i,n}(x)$ using the formula: $B_{i,n}(x) = \frac{2}{(n-i)+1} (1-x)^{n-i} \sum_{k=0}^{n} (-1)^k \binom{2n+1-k}{i-k} \binom{i}{k} x^{i-k}$ (or the equivalent form using non-orthonormal basis $b_{i,n}(x)$).

steps.title: Construct the Approximation Space
steps.instruction: Define the finite-dimensional subspace $V_n$ and the constrained subspace $U_n$ to satisfy the specific boundary conditions of the eigenvalue problem.

substeps.instruction: Define $U_n = \{w \in V_n : w^{(m)}(0) = w^{(m)}(1) = 0, 0 \le m \le q-1\}$ to account for $2k$ boundary conditions.
Select the normalized basis $\phi_j(x) = B_{j,n}(x)$ for $j = q, q+1, \dots, n-q$, ensuring $n \ge 2q$.

steps.title: Formulate the Galerkin Approximation
steps.instruction: Apply the normalized Bernstein-Galerkin approximation to the higher-order eigenvalue problem to transform the differential equation into a linear system.

substeps.instruction: Express the approximate solution as $u_n(x) = \sum_{j=q}^{n-q} c_j \phi_j(x)$.
Set up the inner product $\langle u, w \rangle = \int_0^1 u(x) w(x) \theta(x) dx$ with weight function $\theta(x) = 1$.

Construct the matrices $C$, $G_i$, and $G_0$ where: $c_{jk} = \langle B_{k,n}^{(2q)}, B_{j,n} \rangle$, $g_{jki} = \langle B_{k,n}^{(i)}, B_{j,n} \rangle$, and $g_{jk0} = \langle B_{k,n}, B_{j,n} \rangle$.

steps.title: Solve for Eigenvalues
steps.instruction: Convert the Galerkin approximation into a matrix eigenvalue problem and solve for $\lambda$.

substeps.instruction: Formulate the matrix equation $(C + \sum_{i=1}^{2q-1} \rho_i G_i + \lambda \rho_0 G_0)\xi = 0$.
Simplify to the form $F + \lambda G = 0$, where $F = C + \sum_{i=1}^{2q-1} \rho_i G_i$ and $G = \rho_0 G_0$.
Calculate the eigenvalues using the system $\lambda I = -FG^{-1}$.
